pages.hook: Some colors in the USA are famous all over the world. Yellow taxis, yellow school buses and green dollars all tell a small story about daily life.

facts.label: The dollar bill
facts.sub: People call US paper money “greenbacks”.

facts.label: School buses
facts.sub: Yellow school buses are easy to see, so cars know to stop.

facts.label: The US flag
facts.sub: The flag has 13 stripes and 50 stars.

facts.label: New York City taxis
facts.sub: Yellow taxis are a symbol of the city.

pages.polite: To ask whose it is, say **Excuse me, is this your bag?** Then say **Thanks!**

mythfact.s: School buses in the USA are usually yellow.
mythfact.why: Yellow school buses are the standard in the USA.

mythfact.s: New York City taxis are famous for being purple.
mythfact.why: They are famous for being yellow.

mythfact.s: The US flag has red, white and blue.
mythfact.why: Red, white and blue are the colors of the US flag.

mythfact.s: A “greenback” is a US dollar.
mythfact.why: The back of the bill is green, so the name stuck.

mythfact.s: The poem “The Purple Cow” says the writer saw many purple cows.
mythfact.why: The poet says he never saw one and never hopes to see one.

decode.why: The colors are black, white and green. Red is not there.

compare.br: The Brazilian flag is green, yellow, blue and white. Many Brazilians say “a minha é azul” without repeating the noun.
compare.us: The US flag is red, white and blue. In English you say “mine is blue”: mine, yours, his, hers replace “my bag”, “your bag”.
compare.tip: Say “Is this yours?” and “It’s mine.” You do not need to repeat the noun.
compare.ask: What color is your phone? Say it in English.

quiz.why: Nice color! is short and friendly.

pages.title: Cultural spotlight · Quiz
Reading quest — The red bag at the airport · part 1
text: Lena is at the airport in **Phoenix**. She waits for her bag. Many bags come out on the belt. There are black bags, green bags and blue bags.
A young man points at a red bag. “**Excuse me, is this your bag?**” he asks. “No,” says Lena. “**Mine is blue**. This one is red.” Then she sees her bag. “Oh, **that’s mine**! Thank you!”
The man smiles. “**What color is your phone?**” he asks. It is a strange question, but Lena answers: “It’s black. And yours?” “Mine is white,” he says. “**Nice colors!**”

opts: Finding the right bag at an airport
fast.why: Lena finds her blue bag at the airport.

scan.q: In what year did Gelett Burgess write the poem?

tf.s: Lena is at the airport in Phoenix.
tf.why: “Lena is at the airport in Phoenix.”

tf.s: The red bag is Lena’s.
tf.why: Lena says, “Mine is blue. This one is red.”

tf.s: The young man’s phone is white.
tf.why: “Mine is white,” he says.

tf.s: Lena’s bag is purple.
tf.why: It is a normal blue bag.

order: A man asks about the red bag.
The man takes the red bag and they say goodbye.

ctx.why: Points at = shows with a finger.

ctx.sent: He never saw a purple cow.

pages.title: Reading quest — The red bag at the airport · part 2
text: Lena thinks of a funny poem called “The Purple Cow.” An American writer, Gelett Burgess, wrote it in 1895. He says he **never saw** a purple cow, and he never hopes to see one. “**That’s funny!**” Lena thinks. Her bag is not purple. It is a normal blue, but it is easy to find.
The man takes the red bag. “**Not my color**,” he laughs, “but it is my bag!” Lena says goodbye. “**Take care of your things!**” she says. He smiles and waves.

text: Lena is at the airport in **Phoenix**. She waits for her bag. Many bags come out on the belt. There are black bags, green bags and blue bags.
A young man points at a red bag. “**Excuse me, is this your bag?**” he asks. “No,” says Lena. “**Mine is blue**. This one is red.” Then she sees her bag. “Oh, **that’s mine**! Thank you!”
The man smiles. “**What color is your phone?**” he asks. It is a strange question, but Lena answers: “It’s black. And yours?” “Mine is white,” he says. “**Nice colors!**”

Lena thinks of a funny poem called “The Purple Cow.” An American writer, Gelett Burgess, wrote it in 1895. He says he **never saw** a purple cow, and he never hopes to see one. “**That’s funny!**” Lena thinks. Her bag is not purple. It is a normal blue, but it is easy to find.
The man takes the red bag. “**Not my color**,” he laughs, “but it is my bag!” Lena says goodbye. “**Take care of your things!**” she says. He smiles and waves.

opts: Finding the right bag at an airport
